Definition: to breathe out, i.e. (by implication) expire
BiblicalUsage: Gava means to breathe out, to expire — to give up the ghost. Ishmael gave up the ghost and died and was gathered to his people in Genesis 25:17, and Job wishes he had given up the ghost before any eye saw him in Job 10:18. Achan perished not alone in his iniquity in Joshua 22:20, and the priests and elders gave up the ghost in the city in Lamentations 1:19.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe giving up the ghost is the last breath of every life, and the Bible does not hide it. Ishmael and Job and the priests of Jerusalem all breathed their last, and I hold that the breath God gave returns to God who gave it.
